_README: The pilot: the whole SLURM chain, end to end, on 18 runs and ~37 GB.
It is the same chain, the same code and the same per-node settings as the real
run (config_lrz.json) -- only narrower: 1 job x 2 nodes instead of 2 x 4. So a
green pilot means the 896-core submit is a scale-up, not a leap. Run it, and read
logs/status.txt: it should say COMPLETE, with BAMs in merged/bams/ and a real
WHAT TO ACTUALLY MEASURE -- the pilot exists for this one number:
awk -F'\t' 'NR>1 {print $1, $NF}' merged/mapping_summary.tsv   # and the mb_per_s column
The download rate per run, times the 224 runs the real job holds in flight, is
what says whether the full cohort is bandwidth-bound. It is also the number to
lower `download.connections` on if ENA starts refusing.
_pilot_set: config/pilot_runs.txt -- chosen from the 9,266-run candidates.tsv, not at random:
* 16 STRONG-tier runs, one per STUDY. 18 runs from 18 labs exercise 18 library
protocols; 18 runs from one study would exercise the same one 18 times, and
reading the library architecture out of the reads is the thing most likely to
break on a protocol nobody anticipated.
* stratified 0.22 GB -> 6.34 GB, so the download rate is measured across the
size distribution rather than at one end of it.
* 2 WEAK-tier runs (SRR10142815, SRR4000640), which are there to be REJECTED.
They test the half of the pipeline a happy path never reaches: the QC gate
dropping a run, and merge counting it as 'dropped by QC' -- finished -- rather
than as 'still to do', which would make status.txt ask for a resubmit forever.
Expect roughly 16 BAMs and 2 rejections. Rather fewer BAMs is a finding, not a bug:
strong-tier means the metadata says ribo-seq, and QC is the thing that does not

_slurm._: 1 job x 2 nodes = 224 cores. 2 is the FEWEST cm4_std takes -- there is no 1-node cm4_std job.

project.name: ribomine-pilot
project._: jobs/threads are the REAL run's, deliberately -- a pilot that tests different settings tests nothing. 9 runs land on each node, so only 9 of the 28 slots are ever busy.

pipeline._: start=accessions, so prep splits the list below instead of querying the archive. end=bam: go all the way, on 18 runs.
